sonar-podstawy: Raw, Mid 20°; also compare Wide 47° in shallow water.
Move steadily with the transducer upright. Wide covers more ground; use Narrow 7° when confirming a small target.
Do not choose a rig position from one pass. Repeat the track and check with a lead.
sonar-dno: Raw, same palette and sensitivity on both sides of the boundary; Mid then Narrow.
Make two parallel runs and one cross pass. Compare echo thickness, any second echo and how far the lead sinks.
If the firmer side is clear with a safe landing route, try one rig there and one on the transition.
sonar-materialy: Mid 20° to compare areas; Narrow 7° over a small patch, avoiding a saturated screen.
Mark both sides, repeat the track and feel with a lead for scraping, a dull drop or sediment.
Echo suggests a hardness difference; it cannot distinguish gravel, clay and stone on its own.
sonar-struktury: Wide for the shape of a large feature; Mid for its sides and base.
Run parallel and then across. Record top, side, base and depths.
Choose a point with fish signs, reliable presentation and safe landing, which may be away from the top.
sonar-polozenie: Mid 20° to compare A/B/C; Narrow 7° for the final small target.
Check an edge, firmer patch and quieter alternative. Confirm each waypoint with a second track.
Place a rig only where you can hit the spot repeatedly and land a fish safely.
sonar-potwierdzenie: Do not change palette or sensitivity when comparing the same stretch.
A scan from another direction, lead, observation and map should point to the same area.
If the clues conflict, mark the position uncertain and choose an easier target.
sonar-zielsko: Raw, Mid along the weed edge, Narrow over an opening; lower sensitivity if dense returns hide bottom.
Repeat the track at a right angle and compare plant height and the distance to clear bottom.
Avoid dropping a rig into dense growth. Find a larger opening or outer edge.
sonar-czyste-oczko: Mid 20° to find a gap, Narrow 7° to confirm it.
Make two cross passes, mark boundaries and allow for GPS error and boat drift before checking with a lead.
If the gap is smaller than your repeatable placement area, choose a larger patch.
sonar-ryby: Use Raw rather than relying solely on Fish Icons; Mid for reconnaissance.
Repeat from another direction and compare marks with depth and surface activity.
An arch alone confirms neither carp nor the right place to lay a rig.
sonar-termoklina: Raw, Mid; on deep water adjust depth range so the bottom stays visible.
Compare a horizontal band across tracks and depths; measure temperature and oxygen if you can.
Do not automatically fish the deepest layer without evidence of fish and oxygen.
sonar-mapa: Bait Boat Mode for a bait boat, Boat Mode for a boat; Raw and Wide on the first survey.
Make overlapping parallel passes under 3 km/h, spacing them according to depth and beam width. A cross pass checks structure.
Save A/B/C waypoints, then revisit chosen patches with Mid/Narrow and a lead.
sonar-lodka: Bait Boat Mode, stable Wi-Fi, Raw; Wide for survey, Mid and Narrow on return.
Mount the transducer upright, travel evenly below 3 km/h and avoid sharp turns over the target.
Return from another direction. Wind and GPS error call for care while lowering the rig.
sonar-brzeg: CHIRP+ 2 Onshore Mode and GPS; Raw and Wide to survey, Mid to check.
Cast overlapping fan-shaped tracks in a permitted area, retrieve consistently and mark the edges of changes.
Feel the target with a lead before feeding. Echo time is not an exact distance map.
sonar-ustawienia: Start in the appropriate mode with Raw, Mid 20°, a fixed palette and enough sensitivity to see bottom without a screen full of noise.

Wide 100 kHz/47° for area, Mid 240 kHz/20° for transitions and Narrow 675 kHz/7° for small patches. Reduce noise in weed; on deep water check depth range and raise sensitivity only if weak returns vanish.
There is no universal sensitivity percentage. Save settings alongside a waypoint and compare at the same parameters.
sonar-raw: Use Raw to learn bottom structure. Treat Fish Icons as a secondary clue.
Compare the same track in one palette. Do not raise sensitivity until noise hides bottom.
A fish icon does not establish species; repeat the scan and watch the fish.
sonar-bledy: Check mode, beam, Raw/Basic, palette and depth range before interpreting.
If the image looks odd, slow down, check sonar position and Wi-Fi, then repeat the same track.
Do not change several settings together. Without another check, the conclusion remains a hypothesis.
sonar-checklista: Choose Bait Boat, Boat or Onshore for the mounting method, with Raw and a fixed palette.
Record speed, track, depth, hardness, weed, waypoint and the lead check.
Place a rig only after checking rules, presentation and a safe landing route.
